findings.reason: as written the gate can only pass on the author's own day and every later worker reads a red or unreproducible measure, so the plan must restore a window parameter or compare against a recorded count.
findings.text: the fleet-node check "reproduces §1's imas-cx CONNECTION_CLOSED count within 5% for the same window", but the changed §2 says the census reads only "the last seven days" and the earlier `--since` option was removed, so the census cannot be pointed at §1's window (2026-10-01..10-08) — the count moves with each day's roll-off (~545 connections/day against §1's 1,068), exceeding the 5% band the gate asserts

findings.reason: a worker following §2 finds its named functions cannot count the deliverable, and the "changes nothing" clause removes the one in-scope route to fix it, so the plan must name the tool-result reader or scope its addition.
findings.text: §2 counts storage-slow tool results "through transcript parsing" by naming transcript_index and session_usage, but transcript_index only maps session ids to transcript files and session_usage only sums token usage (reckon/velocity.py:1363, :1384); neither parses tool_result blocks, and the only tool-result reader there (promotion_receipts) counts Bash promotion receipts, not storage-slow — so the named mechanism cannot produce the count — and the same sentence's constraint that the section "changes nothing in velocity.py" forbids adding the function that could

findings.reason: the node cannot satisfy its own done-when within its write scope; it must either add dispatch.py to the write paths or drop the run-record assertion, and a worker left to choose will edit an unowned file or silently skip half the measure.
findings.text: §7's done-when asserts "the run record names it" (the servers enabled), but §7's declared write paths are only reckon/_backends.py and the test, while the run record is composed in reckon/crew/dispatch.py (record.update at dispatch.py:~7945) and the _backends.LaunchPlan returned by launch_plan (reckon/_backends.py:340) carries no field for enabled servers

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited symbol resolves: `_seed_harness_entry` at reckon/_backends.py:2280 (seeded from _backends.py:3203), `transcript_index` at reckon/velocity.py:1363, `session_usage` at reckon/velocity.py:1384, `_run_under_deadline` at reckon/mcp.py:299; the extensionless href `/reckon/reckon-reads-answer-in-seconds` resolves as docs/plans/reckon-reads-answer-in-seconds.html (house convention).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's fleet-node reproduction requires the census to reproduce §1's count "for the same window", but this change removed the `--since` option (§2 now reads only "the last seven days"), so the window §1 measured cannot be selected and the count drifts with log roll-off.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §2 writes tests/test_mcp_census.py, §7 writes tests/test_worker_mcp_servers.py, and the plan's other evidence lands on durable paths (the §4 run directory, §6's reports/reckon/mcp-failures/imas-cx-os-error-2/); no gate writes to a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new symbols (reckon/mcp_census.py, worker_mcp_servers, tests/test_mcp_census.py, tests/test_worker_mcp_servers.py) are named by what they do and carry no plan labels, phase names, ticket numbers or version tags.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2 names transcript_index and session_usage as the mechanism for counting storage-slow tool results, but neither function reads tool results, and §7's done-when asserts the run record names the enabled servers while §7's declared write paths cannot write the run record.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 is one census deliverable (MCP-log causes plus the storage-slow count serve the one "name every failure's cause" goal) and §7 is one deliverable (a worker starts only the servers its work uses).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §7's changed write path (reckon/_backends.py) conflicts with no other section, and §2's shared reckon/cli.py write against §5 is recorded in followup f-amfc-001 ("§5 waits for §2, because both edit reckon/cli.py").
